tools.name: exec_command
tools.description: Runs a command in a PTY, returning output or a session ID for ongoing interaction.

justification.description: User-facing approval question for `require_escalated`; omit otherwise.

login.description: True runs the shell with -l/-i semantics; false disables them. Defaults to true.

max_output_tokens.description: Output token budget. Defaults to 10000 tokens; larger requests may be capped by policy.

prefix_rule.description: Reusable approval prefix for `cmd`, only with `sandbox_permissions: "require_escalated"`; for example ["git", "pull"].

sandbox_permissions.description: Per-command sandbox override. Defaults to `use_default`; use `require_escalated` for unsandboxed execution.

shell.description: Shell binary to launch. Defaults to the user's default shell.

tty.description: True allocates a PTY for the command; false or omitted uses plain pipes.

workdir.description: Working directory for the command. Defaults to the turn cwd.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding output. Defaults to 10000 ms; effective range is 250-30000 ms.

tools.name: write_stdin
tools.description: Writes characters to an existing unified exec session and returns recent output.

chars.description: Bytes to write to stdin. Defaults to empty, which polls without writing.

max_output_tokens.description: Output token budget. Defaults to 10000 tokens; larger requests may be capped by policy.

session_id.description: Identifier of the running unified exec session.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding output. Non-empty writes default to 250 ms and cap at 30000 ms; empty polls wait 5000-300000 ms by default.

tools.name: list_mcp_resources
tools.description: Lists resources provided by MCP servers. Resources allow servers to share data that provides context to language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information. Prefer resources over web search when possible.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous list_mcp_resources call; omit for the first page.

server.description: MCP server name. Omit to list resources from every configured server.

tools.name: list_mcp_resource_templates
tools.description: Lists resource templates provided by MCP servers. Parameterized resource templates allow servers to share data that takes parameters and provides context to language models, such as files, database schemas, or application-specific information. Prefer resource templates over web search when possible.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous list_mcp_resource_templates call; omit for the first page.

server.description: MCP server name. Omit to list resource templates from every configured server.

tools.name: read_mcp_resource
tools.description: Read a specific resource from an MCP server given the server name and resource URI.

server.description: MCP server name exactly as configured. Must match the 'server' field returned by list_mcp_resources.

uri.description: Resource URI to read. Must be one of the URIs returned by list_mcp_resources.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.name: view_image
tools.description: View a local image file from the filesystem when visual inspection is needed. Use this for images already available on disk.

path.description: Local filesystem path to an image file.

tools.description:
# Tool discovery

Searches over deferred tool metadata with BM25 and exposes matching tools for the next model call.

You have access to tools from the following sources:
- Multi-agent tools: Spawn and manage sub-agents.
- aca_fixture
Some of the tools may not have been provided to you upfront, and you should use this tool (`tool_search`) to search for the required tools. For MCP tool discovery, always use `tool_search` instead of `list_mcp_resources` or `list_mcp_resource_templates`.

limit.description: Maximum number of tools to return. Defaults to 8.

tools.name: read_fixture
tools.description: Read the synthetic Coding Access compatibility marker.
